lines: Solen's eyes widen as he reads the relay log. 'Underground movement... thermal signatures not consistent with geological activity...'
'This is extraordinary. The Underlumen — I knew it. Life beneath the surface, using geothermal energy. The planet isn't dead at all.'
'I need more evidence. Survey Marker Delta-7, planted by the original surveyors near the old watchtower. Find it for me, and I'll give you my Resonance Detector prototype.'
The orange tabby purrs and bumps its head against your hand. The collar reads 'EMBER — if found, return to Vell, East Terrace.'
So this is Vell's missing cat. She looks comfortable here — Archivist Solen has clearly been feeding her. You should tell Vell you found her.
The Records Clerk looks up from a stack of transit logs. 'Actually — since you're here. I've been cross-referencing transit logs and something doesn't add up.'
'One of the station couriers, Halden, hasn't filed a cargo manifest in four days. That's not just late — that's unprecedented.'
'Would you ask Station Master Calloway if he's seen Halden? The station is south through the Market Quarter.'
The Records Clerk examines the logbook carefully. 'Torn pages... rerouted shipments... these route codes don't match any authorized transit paths.'
'He was diverting cargo to coordinates outside the city walls. Medical supplies, copper stock, power cells — things the Unbounded traders pay a premium for.'
'I'll file a report with the Civic Center. Here — for your trouble. I found this in the restricted archives last week. It's wasted on a filing clerk.'
Solen looks up with barely-suppressed excitement — and something that might be fear underneath it.
'You were out there. Near the Spire of Vigil. I've been reading the transit logs.' He pushes a stack of archive printouts across the reading table.
'The Spire is pre-Array. Pre-human, if you follow the mineral dating. We always assumed it was a natural formation — the raiders used it as a defensible position and that was that.'
'But if it activated... something powered it. Raiders don't have that technology. Dural Voss is a warlord, not an Array engineer.'
'Whatever activated the Spire used the same resonance frequency as the Lighthouse network. That's not a coincidence. The original architects of one built the other — or they built both.'
'If there are more Spires out there, they may all be connected. And if something is turning them on, we need to find out what — before the next one activates without warning.'
Solen is standing rather than sitting, which he never does. Several archive boxes are open on the floor around him.
'The Spire of Winds. The Compact has been guarding it for a century — calling it a cultural monument, restricting access, logging every visitor.' His voice is very controlled.

'The Compact knew it was a Spire. They had to. The resonance signatures are in the original survey records — those records are in this archive. They requested restricted access thirty-two years ago and I approved it without reading them carefully.'
'I helped them hide it. I didn't know what I was helping hide, but that doesn't—' He stops. Sets down the folder he is holding.
'MERIDIAN-7 is going intermittent. The scholarly consensus is that the Deep Array is responding to the Spire's activation. That means the Array didn't activate it either. So what did?'

'The Compact was guarding something they didn't fully understand. The Array is responding to something it didn't anticipate. And whatever the Spires actually are — they are awake now. We are all standing inside something very old and very large.'
